summary: Bridger-Teton cab in the Wyoming Range, moved in from Red Castles, abandoned by the early 1970s and restored by Sublette County volunteers in 2015-2019.

facts.design: 11 ft x 11 ft single-story Plan 80 cabin
facts.roof_marker: large 8 on the south roof, for identification from the air; the brochure describes it as yellow, the county page describes the restored 8 as white
facts.location: Deadline Ridge in the Wyoming Range, Sublette County, Wyoming

staffing.status: no longer staffed; abandoned as a lookout by the early 1970s

access.note: Open to visitors on Bridger-Teton National Forest land; county open house August 24, 2019; guest book kept inside; rough backcountry roads, high clearance recommended; no restroom, water or other services.

visit.trail_note: About a 45-minute drive southwest of Big Piney on backcountry forest roads; the last stretch is a road of about half a mile to the ridgetop.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Bridger-Teton National Forest (Big Piney Ranger District)

events.note: County page and brochure give 1941 (brochure cites Forest Service records and $483 in FS funds); NHLR gives circa 1940. Brochure says CCC construction was possible but not documented.
Brochure: the structure was moved from the Red Castles site on Bare Pass sometime before 1955; the exact year is not given

Used into the late 1960s (county) or the 1960s and perhaps early 1970s (NHLR); brochure gives use as circa 1941-1964 and says all Bridger-Teton lookouts were abandoned by the early 1970s. Exact year for this site is not given.
Volunteer clean-out and repainting began in August 2015 (Pinedale Online); the brochure dates the project 2016 to 2019
By September 2016 the door and eleven of fifteen windows had been restored and reinstalled
County open house for the restored lookout on August 24, 2019; the county says the project lasted three years

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives circa 1940 and says early 1940s. The county page and the brochure say 1941 from Forest Service records. The brochure says the structure was moved here from Red Castles before 1955, so the 1941 date may refer to the cab rather than to this site. The county page credits the CCC; the brochure says CCC construction was possible but not documented.

Pinedale Online reports volunteer work starting in August 2015; the brochure dates the project 2016 to 2019; the county says it lasted three years. The story gives the start as August 2015 and notes the brochure dates.

corrections.why: The county page and the brochure give 1941 from Forest Service records. The NHLR gives circa 1940. The brochure says the cab was moved here, so a human should decide whether the record should carry the cab date or the site date.

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed: NHLR circa 1940; county page and brochure 1941 (CCC role claimed on the county page, possible but undocumented per the brochure). The brochure says the cab was moved from Red Castles on Bare Pass before 1955, which the NHLR record does not mention. Restoration start: August 2015 (Pinedale) vs 2016-2019 (brochure). Unread leads: a 2020 Pinedale Online piece says built around 1941 by the CCC; a search snippet from npshistory.com (Lookouts, Latrines, and Lodgepole Cabins, hcs-2.pdf) says the lookout is recommended not eligible for the National Register; neither was read or verified. Road access is from a 2019 brochure; check current conditions with the Big Piney Ranger District before publishing visit advice.
